papers.title: Osteo-Compatibility of 3D Titanium Porous Coating Applied by Direct Energy Deposition (DED) for a Cementless Total Knee Arthroplasty Implant: in Vitro and in Vivo Study.
papers.abstract: : Direct energy deposition (DED) technology has gained increasing attention as a new implant surface technology that replicates the porous structure of natural bones facilitating osteoblast colonization and bone ingrowth. However, concerns have arisen over osteolysis or chronic inflammation that could be caused by Cobalt-chrome (CoCr) alloy and Titanium (Ti) nanoparticles produced during the fabrication process. Here, we evaluated whether a DED Ti-coated on CoCr alloy could improve osteoblast colonization and osseointegration in vitro and in vivo without causing any significant side effects. Three types of implant CoCr surfaces (smooth, sand-blasted and DED Ti-coated) were tested and compared. Three cell proliferation markers and six inflammatory cytokine markers were measured using SaOS2 osteoblast cells. Subsequently, X-ray and bone histomorphometric analyses were performed after implantation into rabbit femur. There were no differences between the DED group and positive control in cytokine assays. However, in the 5-bromo-2'-deoxyuridine (BrdU) assay the DED group exhibited even higher values than the positive control. For bone histomorphometry, DED was significantly superior within the 1000 µm bone area. The results suggest that DED Ti-coated metal printing does not affect the osteoblast viability or impair osseointegration in vitro and in vivo. Thus, this technology is biocompatible for coating the surfaces of cementless total knee arthroplasty (TKA) implants.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文评估DED钛涂层在膝关节植入物上的生物相容性，但未涉及力学测试或应力遮挡分析，与用户关注的AM生物医学方向关联性弱。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not include mechanical testing, fatigue analysis, or stress shielding evaluation; it uses DED not LPBF, and focuses solely on biological osseointegration without linking to implant stiffness or stability.

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the biocompatibility of Direct Energy Deposition (DED) Ti coating on CoCr alloy for cementless knee implants.
summary_en.method: In vitro SaOS2 cell assays and in vivo rabbit femur implantation compared smooth, sand-blasted, and DED Ti-coated surfaces.
summary_en.result: DED coating showed comparable or better cell proliferation and bone histomorphometry without adverse inflammatory response.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture and in vivo animal study with histological analysis.
